newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power flat to lower after rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power flat to lower after rally.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. Southwest and Northwest were flat to lower after high temperatures helped boost prices early in the week, trade sources said Wednesday.
"We saw a lot of activity at PV (Palo Verde) early on," said one trader. "But it looks like the higher prices might have spurred some generators to bring units on line."

Forecasts for higher than normal temperatures in parts of the Southwest through the weekend, along with scheduled restrictions on major power lines linking the Northwest to the Southwest were cited as supporting regional prices.
In addition, a 350 MW coal-fired unit at the San Juan generating station in New Mexico is still off-line after shutting late Friday for tube leak repairs. It is expected to restart Thursday.
In the Northwest, a 750 MW unit at the Centralia power plant in Washington also remains down after shutting Monday for unplanned repairs. It is now expected to be up on Friday.
But traders said unchanged offer prices from the Bonneville Power Administration for the third consecutive day put a damper on the Northwest market.
Next-day Mid-Columbia peak prices were last quoted $16.50-17.00, down slightly from Tuesday.
Next-day PV was last quoted $21.00-23.00, down from $23.00-25.00 on Tuesday.
Cash November PV was quoted $17.40-$17.85, while November Mid-Columbia was assessed at $17.05-17.60 and November COB traded at $18.50.
